title: Priming desynchronization causing TTFT spikes across deployments — customer bridge & hotpatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers (two Hosted, one Dedicated, and one Private VPC) reported sudden TTFT regressions and tokens/sec drops after the runtime handshake change deployed 2026-03-09. Observed behavior: short prompts (<=32 tokens) have median TTFT increase from ~85ms to ~420ms and sustained throughput drop ~55% for chat-style requests on quantized 13B variants. Root cause hypothesis: a priming desynchronization between the new microbatch handshake and the KV-cache prefetch path that causes repeated redundant priming and stalls on the first N tokens (priming thrash). This is amplified on Dedicated and Private where per-tenant warmup credits are limited. Impact: customer-facing escalations, increased error budgets for two SLAs, elevated cost due to repeated priming tokens being generated and discarded. Scope: observed across hosted, dedicated, and private, but effect size varies by model family and quantization profile. Models affected: rwd-13B-chat-int8, rwd-13B-chat-int4, and a subset of community 7B variants when served with continuous-batching enabled.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use the customer prompt template used in the escalation (short system + 12-20 token user prompt).
2) Send 200 concurrent short-chat requests with continuous batching and microbatch_handshake=true, sequence length <= 64, to a dedicated cluster with quantized models enabled.
3) Observe first-token latency (TTFT) for the first ~10 requests after a warmup window; median TTFT jumps to >350ms and tokens/sec falls by ~50% compared to pre-deploy baseline.
4) Disable microbatch_handshake or disable KV prefetch: TTFT returns to baseline within 2-3 minutes confirming interaction between handshake and prefetch path.
mitigation: Immediate: rolled back microbatch_handshake flag on hosted and a staged rollback triggered for affected Dedicated clusters. Applied short-term rate-limit throttle (token-surge-dampener) to protect warmup credit exhaustion for Private customers. Provided customer-facing bridge and runbook. Monitoring: added dashboard for priming retries, redundant-prefetch counters, and per-tenant warmup-credit burn rate.
proposed_fix: 1) Introduce a handshake-aware priming backoff: when redundant priming detected for a connection, enforce exponential backoff and skip prefetch for a single warmup window. 2) Add a lightweight in-process dedupe for priming RPCs to avoid duplicate KV loads. 3) Tighten the prefetch circuit-breaker thresholds and track per-tenant priming budget. 4) Backfill unit + integration tests to simulate desynchronized priming paths across microbatch handshake states.
rollout_plan: Canary patch on hosted (runtime-2.4.1-hotfix-priming) to 5% of traffic for 1 hour: watch TTFT, redundant_prefetch_rate, warmup_credit_burn.
If canary stable, push to remaining hosted traffic and to Dedicated control-plane push for one priority cluster then stagger the remaining Dedicated clusters over 4 hours.
For Private: provide operator patch and assist with in-place toggles; default to opt-in patch for air-gapped environments.
Rollback plan: automatic revert if median TTFT > baseline+150ms or redundant_prefetch_rate increases post-deploy.
postmortem: Owner: Miguel Santos. Postmortem draft due 2026-03-18. Required analysis: exact ordering window where handshake+prefetch race occurs, why quantized models amplify the effect, and why Dedicated clusters with limited warmup credits deteriorate faster. Action items: instrument per-connection state transitions, add test harness that replays priming races, and propose conservative defaults for microbatch_handshake until handshake-aware priming is validated.
